subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw first keep the app-server path and investigate the server/app-server 429, or build direct-runtime Codex Harmony tool-call support as the supported fallback path?
rationale: Both approaches can plausibly solve the user-visible failure, but the choice changes runtime ownership, provider routing, and tool-call parsing behavior, so automation should not select it without maintainer intent and live proof.

options.title: Investigate app-server first
options.body: Keep the Codex app-server as the default, finish the bookkeeping fix, and require live proof of the server/app-server false-429 before changing routing.

options.title: Add direct Harmony adapter
options.body: Implement Codex Harmony tool-call extraction in the direct OpenAI runtime, then consider an explicit direct fallback only after real tool-call proof.

options.title: Wait for stronger repro
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers or the reporter can provide redacted logs or a repeatable live quota trace.

recommendation.title: Investigate app-server first
recommendation.body: Keep the Codex app-server as the default, finish the bookkeeping fix, and require live proof of the server/app-server false-429 before changing routing.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across Codex app-server harness, auth-profile state, and provider stream compatibility surfaces.
